mechanisms.name: Right-click mover → jump straight to that element's settings
mechanisms.how_it_works: Right-clicking any mover opens the options window pre-navigated to that exact element's config section (size, opacity, fonts, visibility conditions). Spatial selection is the entry point to deep configuration — you never hunt a settings tree for the thing you're pointing at.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Right-click (or a gear on hover) on any pane in edit mode opens that pane's settings directly — opacity, font scale, auto-hide behavior, which tick/timestamp it parks to. Never make the user find the pane by name in a global settings panel.

notable_states: Movers shown vs hidden is orthogonal to the options window being open — you can drag with options closed
Per-element temporary hide (Shift+right-click) creates a 'peek under' sub-state within edit mode
Profiles are exportable as text strings and per-character, layered over the mover positions
traps: ElvUI's full options tree is notoriously overwhelming (hundreds of toggles across dozens of tabs); its usability survives only because movers give spatial entry. Do not build a StudyLoop settings tree that requires naming panes — but also don't ship ElvUI-scale option density at all.

Movers-always-labeled works because WoW pauses nothing; but ElvUI has no live preview of conditional states (combat fade etc.) inside move mode — users must leave, trigger combat, and return. StudyLoop should simulate states (hover chrome visible, heatmap on) inside edit mode instead.

products.name: Final Fantasy XIV HUD Layout editor

mechanisms.name: Stepped element scaling via a single cycling shortcut
mechanisms.how_it_works: With an element selected (gold outline), Ctrl+Home (R3 on controller) cycles the element through a small set of discrete preset sizes (e.g. 60/80/90/100/120/140%) rather than free resize handles. Community layouts routinely use graduated scales (hotbar 1 at 90%, bar 2 at 80%, bar 3 at 60%) to encode importance. Arrow keys move a selected panel one pixel at a time to avoid drag overshoot.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Offer stepped size presets per pane (S/M/L cycling on a single key) instead of — or in addition to — free-form corner dragging. Discrete steps keep every layout looking intentional and make 'importance hierarchy via scale' trivially achievable; free resize is what produces ragged, slightly-off layouts.

mechanisms.name: Per-element settings sheet: opacity, visibility, layering from right-click
mechanisms.how_it_works: Right-clicking any HUD element (or the cog) opens UI Element Settings: a transparency slider, a 'Display Element' checkbox, and layer order. Hidden elements do not disappear from the editor — they turn purple and stay draggable, so you always know what's off and can re-enable it in place. Shift-drag snaps elements to grid lines.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Per-pane opacity slider is table stakes for text-over-footage — FFXIV proves users tune each element's transparency individually. Steal the purple-ghost pattern: a disabled pane stays visible in edit mode as a tinted ghost rather than vanishing into a hidden list.

mechanisms.name: Four numbered layout slots with copy-between-slots
mechanisms.how_it_works: The editor header has 4 numbered tabs, each a complete independent HUD layout, switchable in-game via a text command (and therefore bindable/macroable). The HUD Layout Settings cog lets you copy any slot onto another as a starting point. Players keep e.g. a combat layout, a crafting layout, a screenshot-clean layout.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: A small fixed number of named layout slots (Watch / Drill / Review) beats an unbounded list. Make slot-switch a first-class hotkey during playback, and make 'duplicate this slot then diverge' the primary creation flow — nobody builds a second layout from scratch.

notable_states: HUD Layout mode is a full modal screen state; the game world keeps rendering behind it as live preview
Selected element: gold outline; hidden element: purple tint but still present and movable
Element category pulldowns (Basic / System / Hotbars / Duty) let you select tiny or overlapping elements you cannot easily click
traps: No free-form pixel snapping guidance beyond hold-Shift grid snap — players resort to arrow-key pixel nudging for alignment, and 'more precise HUD' is a perennial official-forum request. Ship magnetism from day one; don't make pixel-nudging the primary precision tool.
Discrete size steps with no in-between caused its own complaint class (elements that are right at 80% but wrong at 100%). If StudyLoop uses stepped sizes, allow a fine-adjust escape hatch.
Layout slots are numbered, not named, so players keep external notes about which slot is which. Name the slots.

products.name: RaceLab (sim-racing overlays; SimHub as comparison point)

mechanisms.name: Lock toggle = the entire edit/play boundary
mechanisms.how_it_works: Each overlay window has exactly two states flipped by a lock icon or Ctrl+Shift+L: unlocked (opaque-ish, draggable, resizable, catches the mouse) and locked (transparent chrome, completely click-through — mouse events pass to the game underneath). Position is remembered automatically the moment you drag; there is no explicit save step for placement.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: The click-through property is the key idea: in play mode, StudyLoop panes should be visually present but interaction-transparent by default (clicks reach the video/seek bar underneath), with hover re-arming their chrome. One global lock shortcut that flips all panes between editable and click-through is the effortless version of edit mode.

mechanisms.name: Layout as a single spanning canvas containing many overlays
mechanisms.how_it_works: A RaceLab layout is one big window spanning all monitors into which you place, resize, and stack any number of overlays; it is saved as a profile, multiple exist, one active at a time. This contrasts with loose per-overlay windows, which each remember position independently — the layout bundles the whole arrangement into one switchable object.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Treat the whole console arrangement as one persisted object (a layout), not per-pane saved positions. Per-pane persistence (SimHub-style) makes 'switch my whole setup' impossible; a layout object makes it one action and makes sharing/exporting trivial.

mechanisms.name: Auto-switching layouts by context selectors
mechanisms.how_it_works: Layouts carry selectors (which car, which racing series, etc.); when the sim reports a matching context, RaceLab activates the right layout automatically — the driver never opens a menu mid-session.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Bind layouts to content context: video source/type (lecture vs BJJ instructional), or player state (paused vs playing, quiz active). E.g. pausing could auto-activate the note-dense layout; entering spaced-review auto-activates the minimal quiz layout. Choreograph the switch, don't menu it.

notable_states: Per-overlay locked (click-through, transparent) vs unlocked (draggable) — independently toggleable but usually flipped globally
Layout active vs inactive; only one layout live at a time, switched manually or by selector match
Overlays can auto-open on app start, so the 'session begins configured' state is the norm
traps: SimHub's equivalent has no per-game overlay profiles — overlays are globally on or off — and it is a top user complaint (GitHub issue #2144). Context-blind layouts force manual reconfiguration every session; StudyLoop must scope layouts to context from the start.

Racing overlays are unbounded in count and users pile them on until the track is invisible; RaceLab docs push restraint via setup tips instead of enforcing it. StudyLoop should cap simultaneous panes or degrade opacity as density rises — the video is the point.

Fully invisible-when-locked chrome means users forget an overlay exists and can't find how to unlock it (support docs exist for 'layout on wrong screen'). Always keep one discoverable affordance (a cabinet handle, a keyboard shortcut hint) for re-entering edit mode.

products.name: Apple Vision Pro / visionOS window management (video apps)

mechanisms.name: Chrome appears only where you look: window bar and corner-radius resize
mechanisms.how_it_works: A window shows no persistent manipulation chrome. Look at the bottom of a window and a horizontal 'window bar' materializes — pinch-drag it to move in 3D. Look at a bottom corner and a curved corner handle appears — pinch-drag it to resize. Look away and both fade. Controls are summoned by attention, scoped to the exact edge that owns the operation, and self-dismissing.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: This is the strongest precedent for StudyLoop's 'chrome appears on hover' principle: give each pane a single move affordance (a slim bottom bar) and a single resize affordance (one curved corner), both faded in by pointer proximity and gone otherwise. One handle per operation, always in the same place, beats eight resize handles and a title bar.

mechanisms.name: Lock to space / anchor to surface, persistent across sessions
mechanisms.how_it_works: A window can be locked to a spot in the room or anchored to a vertical surface like a wall; it stays there as you move around and is still there when you leave and re-enter the room — placement is durable environmental state, not per-launch state.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: The analog of 'anchor to a wall' is StudyLoop's concept-parks-to-timestamp-tick: a pane anchored to a moment in the timeline rather than to screen space. Make anchoring a first-class alternative to floating — a note can be screen-anchored (follows you) or time-anchored (lives at its tick, surfaces when playback approaches). And persist all placement implicitly; visionOS has no 'save layout' button for this.

mechanisms.name: Global size preference instead of per-window fiddling
mechanisms.how_it_works: Settings → Display → Appearance offers Small/Medium/Large/Extra Large, scaling default window and control sizes system-wide, so most users never resize individual windows at all.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Ship a single global density/scale control (affecting default pane size, font size, tick hit-targets) so most learners never touch per-pane sizing. Per-element controls are the escape hatch, not the primary path.

notable_states: Attention states: window idle (no chrome) → gazed (bar/corner visible) → grabbed (moving/resizing) — a three-stage escalation with no explicit mode switch
Immersive video (Environments/docked player) vs floating-window video are distinct modes with different control grammars
Spatial persistence: layouts survive leaving/re-entering the physical room
traps: visionOS has no save/restore of multi-window arrangements and no snapping or alignment between windows — a top developer-forum feedback item ('Improve windows management on Vision Pro'). Attention-summoned chrome is worth copying; the absence of layout persistence and magnetism is not.

Gaze-summoned controls fail when the affordance is where you aren't looking — users report hunting for the resize corner. In a 2D app, tie appearance to generous proximity zones, not exact hover on a 4px handle.

No numeric/precise placement exists at all; everything is freehand. Fine for ambient windows, fatal for a study console where a pane must clear the seek bar — keep the nudge/snap layer from the game-HUD lineage.

niches.niche_summary: Mature HUD editors converge on one architecture StudyLoop should adopt wholesale: a hard edit/play boundary where play mode is click-through and chrome-free (RaceLab's lock, WoW's Edit Mode) and edit mode materializes EVERYTHING — including normally-hidden elements — as labeled, draggable ghosts (ElvUI movers, FFXIV's purple hidden-element tint). Effortlessness comes from layered precision that costs nothing up front: magnetic edge-snapping between elements by default, optional grid with adjustable spacing, then a nudge box with 1px arrows and numeric coordinates for the last mile (drag-only editors like FFXIV's are the ones users call fiddly). Layouts are single serializable objects — named slots, duplicated-then-diverged rather than built from scratch, exported as clipboard strings, and auto-switched by context (WoW's per-spec layouts, RaceLab's selectors) so the right arrangement appears without a menu. The spatial-computing branch adds the presentation grammar the game editors lack: attention-summoned single-purpose handles (visionOS window bar and corner) and anchoring panes to a place in the content rather than the screen — but visionOS also proves that gaze-summoned chrome without snapping, persistence, or numeric placement collapses into frustration, so the two lineages must be combined, not chosen between.

products.name: Scrimba (interactive 'scrim' screencasts)

mechanisms.name: Pause-to-fork: the frozen frame is a live workspace
mechanisms.how_it_works: A scrim is not pixels — it is a recorded event stream of editor state. Pressing spacebar pauses playback and the 'video frame' instantly becomes a fully editable, runnable code environment at exactly that point in the lesson. The learner edits, runs, breaks things, then presses play; the scrim discards (or optionally saves as a personal snapshot) their divergence and resumes the instructor's timeline from the pause point. There is zero mode-switch ceremony — pause IS edit mode.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: This is the strongest generate-first pattern in existence. On pause, StudyLoop's overlay panes should become 'hot': the attempt pane opens pre-seeded with the current timestamp's context, the learner writes their answer/drill-plan against the frozen frame, and pressing play folds their attempt into a parked tick on the seek bar and resumes footage. Pause = attempt state, play = instructor state, with the divergence saved as an artifact.

mechanisms.name: Timeline as event log, not media
mechanisms.how_it_works: Because the recording is events, seeking is state reconstruction: scrubbing to any point rebuilds the exact editor state there. Learner edits are diffs against a timeline position, so 'my version at 12:40' is a first-class addressable object.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Model learner artifacts (notes, attempts, drawings) as diffs anchored to timeline positions, so scrubbing to a tick reconstructs 'what I knew/tried at this moment' — the pane contents rehydrate per-timestamp rather than being one global notepad.

notable_states: Playing (instructor timeline authoritative)
Paused-editing (learner authoritative, timeline frozen)
Resumed-after-edit (learner divergence discarded or snapshotted, instructor state restored)
traps: Only works because content is authored in-format; StudyLoop ingests arbitrary video, so do not promise 'edit the frame' — steal the pause-is-attempt-mode grammar, not the event-stream substrate.
Scrimba's blank-slate pause can strand beginners with no scaffold; StudyLoop's pause-attempt pane must always offer a prompt, never an empty void.

products.name: Bilibili / Niconico danmaku (bullet comments)

mechanisms.name: Time-anchored comments rendered ON the footage, density as signal
mechanisms.how_it_works: Every comment is bound to a video timestamp and flies right-to-left across the frame at that moment (or pins top/bottom). Density is the emotional/attention heatmap made visible: climactic moments produce a wall of text. Viewers get granular controls: an on/off master toggle on the player chrome, opacity slider, display-area limiter (e.g. restrict to top 25% of frame), speed, font size, and keyword/user filters. Hovering a flying comment pauses that comment (not the video) and reveals like/report/copy actions.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Two steals: (1) render the learner's own past notes as ephemeral fly-bys or fade-ins at their anchored timestamp during rewatch — memory resurfacing choreographed by the timeline, honoring spaced review without opening a pane; (2) the display-area limiter and opacity slider are the right control vocabulary for StudyLoop's holographic overlays — a single 'overlay pressure' slider governing how much of the frame annotations may claim.

mechanisms.name: Comment-density curve as a second heatmap channel
mechanisms.how_it_works: Danmaku density over time is effectively a crowd-attention histogram; Bilibili surfaces spikes ('high-energy moments') and some clients chart density under the seek bar.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Overlay note-density (where the learner annotated most) as a second channel on the attention heatmap — 'where I engaged' vs 'where I replayed' are different curves and their divergence flags passively-rewatched-but-never-processed sections.

notable_states: Danmaku on / off / area-limited (top-N% of frame reserved clear)
Individual comment hovered (comment frozen, video still playing)
traps: Unbounded density destroys the footage — danmaku regularly occludes the entire frame. StudyLoop must cap simultaneous on-frame text and never let resurfaced notes cover the region of instructional interest.
Constant motion of flying text steals attention from the video itself; for study (vs entertainment), prefer fade-in-place at the anchor over horizontal flight.

products.name: Descript (transcript-first video editing)

mechanisms.name: Transcript IS the transport: word-level bidirectional cursor
mechanisms.how_it_works: The transcript is the primary editing surface. Clicking any word seeks the video to that word; playing the video moves a highlight cursor through the text word-by-word. Selecting a text range selects the corresponding media range; deleting words deletes video. Every operation the timeline supports is expressible as a text operation.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: StudyLoop's transcript pane should be a full transport peer, not a read-along: click-word-to-seek, select-sentence-to-set-loop-range, and highlight-text-to-create-a-parked-concept (the tick lands at the first word's timestamp with the selection as its excerpt). Range selection in text is far more precise than drag handles on a seek bar for lecture content.

mechanisms.name: Composition markers / slash-commands inside the text stream
mechanisms.how_it_works: Typing markers directly into the transcript (e.g. slash-commands) drops named markers that appear simultaneously in the timeline; the text document and timeline are two projections of one model.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Let learners type an inline token in the notes pane (e.g. '@@drill') that instantly parks a typed tick on the seek bar at current time — annotation as a typing side-effect, no mouse trip, matching Frame.io's I/O-while-typing pattern but text-native.

notable_states: Text-cursor-driven playback (video follows the caret)
Playback-driven text highlight (caret follows the video)
traps: Descript makes text so primary the footage becomes a preview thumbnail; StudyLoop's contract is edge-to-edge video, so the transcript must live in a cabinet/pane, never become the page.
Word-level sync depends on ASR quality; on noisy BJJ-gym audio the word cursor will jitter — degrade gracefully to sentence-level anchors rather than showing wrong-word highlighting.

products.name: Amazon Prime Video X-Ray

mechanisms.name: Pause as an information event
mechanisms.how_it_works: Pausing (or summoning controls) slides in a contextual panel keyed to the current scene: who is on screen right now, what music is playing, trivia. It is scene-scoped, not video-scoped — the payload changes as the timestamp changes. Tapping an entry expands a side sheet (actor filmography, full soundtrack) without leaving the player; pressing play collapses everything and returns the clean frame. Zero manual lookup: the system pre-indexed the timeline against a knowledge base.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Make pause a semantic event in StudyLoop: on pause, the overlay surfaces the concepts whose time-ranges cover the playhead — their names, the learner's prior notes on them, related ticks elsewhere in the video, and due review items. Play instantly retracts it. This gives the 'holographic' pane system a default, automatic content source with no user effort, and turns idle pauses into free review impressions.

notable_states: Playing (clean frame, X-Ray hidden)
Paused (scene-scoped info panel, deep-dive side sheet available)
traps: X-Ray fires on every pause with no suppression, which trains users to disable it; StudyLoop's pause-context must be dismissible-per-session and must not animate in when the user paused merely to look at the frame (delay ~500ms before appearing).
It is read-only trivia — a dead end with no capture affordance. StudyLoop's version must let every surfaced item be acted on (open note, start review, jump to tick).

products.name: mpv (power-user transport grammar)

mechanisms.name: Single-key cycling A-B loop
mechanisms.how_it_works: One key ('l') cycles a tri-state: first press sets loop point A at the playhead, second press sets B and looping begins immediately, third press clears. No dialog, no drag handles, no mode — the loop is defined while watching, in rhythm with the footage. Loop points render as marks on the OSC seek bar.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: This is the correct drill-loop primitive for BJJ instructionals: one key taps A at the start of a movement, taps B at the end, and the segment loops for physical rehearsal; third tap releases. Persist the last N loops as faint bracket marks on the seek bar so a drilled segment can be re-summoned — a loop is a proto-concept and should be promotable to a parked tick.

mechanisms.name: Frame-step with held-key auto-repeat and precise back-step
mechanisms.how_it_works: '.' and ',' step exactly one frame forward/back and pause; holding the key auto-repeats into a slow crawl, releasing stops. Combined with '[' ']' speed multipliers and backspace to reset speed, the transport is fully keyboard-resident.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Adopt hold-to-crawl frame stepping for mechanics study (grip details, guard transitions). Speed changes must be single keystrokes with a one-key reset — never a settings menu.

mechanisms.name: Scriptable OSD layers and sub-seek
mechanisms.how_it_works: Lua/JS scripts draw arbitrary OSD overlays (ASS-rendered text/shapes) above footage, keyed to properties like time-pos; 'sub-seek' jumps playback to the previous/next subtitle line, treating the annotation track as the navigation unit.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Sub-seek generalizes to tick-seek: one key to jump playhead to previous/next parked concept, making the learner's own annotation layer the primary navigation lattice.

traps: mpv's grammar is invisible — zero discoverability, learned only from the manual. StudyLoop must show a transient keycap hint the first times a mechanism is reachable, then go silent.
Everything is session-scoped (loops and settings evaporate on close); StudyLoop must persist loop marks and speed preferences per-video.

products.name: Chessable video-sync (video + interactive board)

mechanisms.name: Bidirectional sync between video and a parallel interactive artifact
mechanisms.how_it_works: A chess board sits beside the video and plays moves in lockstep as the author discusses them; simultaneously the variation list filters to whatever line the video is currently covering. In reverse, any variation in the list has a 'Jump to video' affordance that seeks the video to where the author discusses exactly that line. The learner can pause, take over the board, explore their own moves (even with engine on), then resync to the video's line.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: The pattern is 'structured knowledge object with two-way timestamp bindings.' StudyLoop's concept cabinet should behave identically: as video plays, the concept list auto-filters/highlights to what is being taught now; every concept card carries a jump-to-video control; and during pause the learner can 'take over' a concept (edit, extend, attempt) before resyncing. For BJJ, the parallel artifact could be the position/technique tree instead of a chess board.

notable_states: Synced (board and list follow video)
Diverged (learner exploring own variation, video paused, resync affordance visible)
traps: Sync only exists because authors hand-tag every variation's video range — expensive authoring. StudyLoop must derive concept↔range bindings from its analysis engine, with cheap learner correction, or the feature never populates.
Chessable splits screen 50/50, shrinking the video permanently; StudyLoop must keep the artifact in a summonable cabinet, not a fixed split.

products.name: Apple Music Sing / modern synced-lyrics players

mechanisms.name: Sub-line (syllable/word) progressive highlighting as a time cursor
mechanisms.how_it_works: Lyrics render as large text over a blurred artwork background; the current line is full-opacity while past/future lines recede in scale and opacity, and within the current line each syllable fills with highlight exactly on the beat. The lyric sheet auto-scrolls so the active line stays at a fixed focal position; tapping any line seeks audio to it. Duet/background vocal lines render on opposite sides or smaller, encoding structure typographically.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: For the bare-floating-text-over-footage mechanism: when a transcript line or instructor cue floats on the frame, animate a subtle progressive fill through it synced to speech — the text itself becomes the fine-grained playhead, and the learner's eye never drops to the seek bar. The recede-past/preview-next typographic stack (previous line ghosted above, next line ghosted below) is the right minimal chrome for a floating transcript.

mechanisms.name: Continuous stem slider (adjustable vocals)
mechanisms.how_it_works: A vertical slider appears on tracks supporting vocal isolation; dragging it attenuates the vocal stem in real time from full to near-mute, letting the user take over the part while the rest keeps playing.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: The generalization is 'attenuate the expert layer continuously, not on/off': a slider that fades instructor overlay text/answers from fully shown to fully hidden supports graduated generate-first practice — the learner dials down the scaffold as recall improves, mirroring the blur-to-reveal pattern but continuous.

traps: Full-screen lyric mode obliterates the visual; StudyLoop floats text over footage, so it must cap simultaneous lines at ~1-2 and keep fill-animation subtle or it competes with the demonstration.
Syllable timing is hand-authored by Apple's pipeline; with ASR-derived timing, downgrade to word- or phrase-level fill rather than showing wrong syllable sync.

products.name: Twitch Extensions (overlay/component slot system)

mechanisms.name: Slot taxonomy with viewer-side kill switches
mechanisms.how_it_works: Extensions mount into declared slots: Overlay (a transparent full-player iframe stacked over video, exactly one allowed), Component (docked widgets along the video edge, launchable/hideable per-viewer via small edge icons), and Panel (below the player). Viewers can individually hide components by clicking their launch icon, and player settings can disable extensions wholesale. Overlay extensions are click-through except where they draw interactive regions, and Twitch's design guidelines require them to honor the player chrome's auto-hide: when controls fade, extension UI is expected to fade too.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Formalize StudyLoop's pane system the same way: a single full-frame 'overlay' layer (holographic text, drawings) plus edge-docked 'components' (cabinets) each with an always-reachable per-pane collapse control on the frame edge, and one global kill switch that clears every overlay to bare video. Bind overlay opacity lifecycle to the same timer that hides player chrome so the whole HUD breathes as one organism.

notable_states: Chrome-visible (overlay UI shown) vs chrome-hidden (overlay fades with controls)
Component collapsed to edge icon vs expanded
traps: Overlay extensions routinely intercept clicks meant for the player (pause becomes a misclick on an invisible hitbox) — StudyLoop overlays must be click-through by default, interactive only within visible bounds.
Streamer-installed clutter with no spatial coordination between extensions; StudyLoop's layout engine must own placement so panes never overlap each other or captions.

products.name: TikTok / CapCut timed text-overlay conventions

mechanisms.name: Per-element lifetime bars in the timeline editor
mechanisms.how_it_works: In the CapCut/TikTok editor, every text sticker gets its own strip under the scrub bar; dragging the strip's end handles sets exactly when that text exists on screen. On the canvas, direct manipulation is the whole grammar: drag to move, pinch/corner-handle to scale-rotate as one gesture, tap to edit content, with snap guides to center/thirds. Playback then shows text entering and leaving at its set times.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: StudyLoop's floating annotations need a lifetime, not just a birth timestamp: when a learner parks a note on the frame, give its seek-bar tick a subtle draggable extent (default: current shot/sentence) controlling when the floating text is present during rewatch. Corner-handle unified scale-rotate is also the right resize grammar for holographic panes — no separate rotate mode.

mechanisms.name: Karaoke-style auto-captions with active-word emphasis
mechanisms.how_it_works: Auto-captions render as bold outlined text with the currently-spoken word scaled up or color-popped, one short phrase at a time, positioned in the safe zone; viewers can tap captions to expand a full transcript sheet.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: Tap-the-floating-caption-to-open-full-transcript is a clean promotion path from ambient text layer to the transcript cabinet — the on-frame text is the handle for the deeper pane.

traps: TikTok text conventions optimize for attention capture (constant scale-pulsing, emoji, hard colors) — hostile to sustained study; steal the timing/manipulation grammar, never the visual style.
Safe-zone chaos: platform UI regularly covers creator text; StudyLoop controls its own chrome, so define hard no-annotation reserves (captions region, seek bar strip) and enforce them at drop time.

products.name: YouTube Ambient Mode (frame-sampled environmental glow)

mechanisms.name: Chrome lit by the footage
mechanisms.how_it_works: In dark theme, YouTube samples dominant colors from the current frames and diffuses them as a soft, slowly-animating gradient glow into the page background around the player, updating continuously as content changes. It is purely ambient — no interaction, subtle enough to miss consciously.
mechanisms.steal_for_studyloop: For a holographic overlay system, derive pane tint/border glow from sampled frame colors so panes read as emitted by the footage rather than pasted over it — the cheapest possible route to the 'hologram' feel. Also usable semantically: warm the glow during flagged high-attention segments as a peripheral, non-textual cue.

traps: Continuous canvas sampling costs GPU/battery and can jank scrubbing on low-end machines — sample at low frequency (1-2 Hz) with long cross-fades, and disable during drag-scrub.
Ambient tinting of interactive elements can crush text contrast; glow must apply to pane borders/backdrops only, never behind body text without a contrast guard.

gaps.niche_summary: The surveyed five niches covered annotation, coaching, mining, quizzing, and HUD editing, but missed the products that dissolve the boundary between the video and the study artifact itself. The biggest blind spots: Scrimba proves pause can BE attempt-mode (the frozen frame becomes a workspace, which is StudyLoop's generate-first pedagogy already industrialized); Descript and Chessable prove the transcript/knowledge-object can be a full bidirectional transport peer rather than a sidebar; and danmaku culture proves time-anchored text rendered on the footage — with density controls and area limiters — is a mature, viewer-governed medium, directly informing both the holographic text layer and a second heatmap channel. On the mechanics side, mpv's single-key cycling A-B loop and annotation-unit seeking is the correct drill grammar for physical-skill study, Prime X-Ray shows pause should be a semantic event that surfaces timestamp-scoped context automatically, and Twitch's overlay/component slot taxonomy plus Apple Music Sing's progressive text-fill and continuous scaffold-attenuation slider supply the missing choreography rules for a HUD that breathes with the player chrome instead of fighting the footage.
